inline_comments.comment: The project convention is `super().__init__(...)` rather than calling the parent class by name (`MolecularDynamics.__init__(self, ...)`). This avoids hardcoding the MRO and is safer if the class hierarchy ever changes. Replace with `super().__init__(atoms=atoms, timestep=timestep, **kwargs)`.

`MaskedMTKNPT.__init__` calls `MolecularDynamics.__init__` directly and then manually re-initializes every attribute that `MTKNPT.__init__` already sets (`_num_atoms_global`, `_thermostat`, `_barostat`, `_temperature_K`, `_pressure_au`, `_kT`, `_q`, `_p`, `_h`). This is full duplication of the parent constructor and creates a maintenance hazard: any future addition to `MTKNPT.__init__` will silently be absent from `MaskedMTKNPT`. The fundamental obstacle is that `MTKNPT.__init__` calls `_init_cell_momenta()` which tries to set `self._p_g = np.zeros((3, 3))` — but the subclass's property setter blocks that. One clean approach: call `super().__init__(...)` normally, initialize `_h0_basis` and `_p_c` afterwards, and override `_init_cell_momenta` in `MaskedMTKNPT` to populate `_p_c` instead. This eliminates duplication while keeping the property guard.

The `_p_g` setter raises a bare `AttributeError()` with no message. If any inherited method (or future code) accidentally tries to assign `self._p_g = ...`, the resulting traceback gives no indication of why the attribute is read-only. Add a descriptive message: `raise AttributeError("_p_g is a computed property on MaskedMTKNPT; update _p_c instead")`.

`_h0_basis` is computed once from the initial cell and is never refreshed during the simulation. Correctness relies on the assumption that lattice vector *directions* do not change — only their magnitudes vary — so that the initial unit vectors remain valid throughout the trajectory. This is guaranteed by the physics only if the inherited `_integrate_cell` propagates the cell using `_p_g`, whose off-diagonal terms are kept zero by the mask. While the assumption holds in the current implementation, it is fragile and completely undocumented. Add an inline comment explaining the assumption, e.g.: `# _h0_basis is fixed: the masked integrator only scales lattice magnitudes, never rotates vectors.`

Using a bare `assert` for argument validation in production code is fragile — assertions are disabled when Python is run with the `-O` flag. Replace with an explicit `if`/`raise ValueError(...)` guard: `if self.masses.shape != (len(self.atoms), 1): raise ValueError(f'Unexpected masses shape: {self.masses.shape}')`.

The `tuple[bool, bool, bool]` annotation uses the built-in generic form available only in Python 3.9+. The existing codebase uses `Tuple` from `typing` for type hints. Use `Tuple[bool, bool, bool]` imported from `typing` for consistency.

The `mask: tuple[bool, bool, bool] | None = None` parameter in `MTKBarostat.__init__` uses the `|` union syntax introduced in Python 3.10. The project targets Python versions where this syntax is not supported and enforces `Union` from `typing` for annotations. Use `Optional[Tuple[bool, bool, bool]]` (or `Union[Tuple[bool, bool, bool], None]`) instead.

The class docstring does not mention that `MaskedMTKNPT(mask=(True, True, True))` is *not* equivalent to `MTKNPT`. With all three axes enabled, `MaskedMTKNPT` has 3 degrees of freedom for cell fluctuations (diagonal elements only), while `MTKNPT` has 9 (full 3×3). This affects the barostat mass `W` and the thermostat target energy, and can produce different sampling even at identical settings. The `MTKBarostat` docstring already notes this distinction, but a reader of `MaskedMTKNPT` alone would not see it. Add a `Note` or `Warning` section to the `MaskedMTKNPT` docstring spelling out this difference.

`test_masked_npt` does not parametrize over `tloop` or `ploop`. The sibling `test_anisotropic_barostat` already parametrizes `ploop`, and varying the number of sub-steps is the main way to catch integration-loop bugs. Consider adding `@pytest.mark.parametrize("ploop", [1, 3])` (and analogously for `tloop`) to `test_masked_npt` for better coverage, or add a comment explaining why those parameters are deliberately excluded.

There are two problems with the bullet text:
1. **Mismatched backticks**: `` `MaskedMTKNPT`` `` has one opening backtick and two closing backticks, which is invalid RST. Use either a Sphinx cross-reference `` :class:`MaskedMTKNPT` `` or a plain inline-code literal ` ``MaskedMTKNPT`` `.
2. **Missing MR reference**: The project convention requires each changelog bullet to end with `(:mr:\`NNNN\`)`. Add the merge request number once it is known.

general_comments.comment: `MaskedMTKNPT` is not registered in `doc/ase/md.rst` with an `.. autoclass::` directive. Per project rules, every new MD integrator class must appear in the NPT section of that file (with a brief description and cross-reference notes where appropriate). Without this, the class is invisible to users reading the official documentation and will not appear in generated API docs.

The `_p_g` property is called from multiple inherited methods (`_integrate_p`, `_integrate_cell`, `_integrate_q`) on every half-step, recomputing three outer-product matrices each time. Caching the result and invalidating when `_p_c` changes (e.g., using `functools.cached_property` with manual invalidation, or simply recomputing once at the top of `step()`) would remove the redundant allocation. This is a minor concern for research-scale runs but worth noting for production trajectories.

The test `test_anisotropic_npt` now correctly passes `tchain=tchain` and `pchain=pchain` to the `MTKNPT` constructor (which was apparently missing before this MR). This incidental fix is good, but it should be called out explicitly — ideally as a separate commit or a comment in the changelog — so reviewers do not need to rediscover why the test was previously silently under-testing those parameters.
